_comment: Inline testing — wire ONE surface with a real exit code + remove the PHP eval RCE.
Feature 132, INLINE-DEC-01 / INLINE-DEC-02.
Tina4 advertises a batteries-included inline test surface: decorate a function
with test expectations and run them all with `tina4 test`. The audit found the
flow did not work end-to-end anywhere -- the CLI ran pytest / phpunit / a file
runner and never the inline runner (Python/PHP/Node), or ran only the describe/it
surface (Ruby). Every case here runs the REAL `tina4 <lang> test` CLI as a child
process against a real throwaway project and asserts the REAL process exit code
and REAL filesystem side effects -- NO MOCKS. See
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/132-inline-testing.md and
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/OWNER-DECISIONS.md (Batch 5, INLINE-DEC-01/02).
INLINE-DEC-01 (the headline fix): the chosen surface is the decorator/@tests
descriptor model. `tina4 <lang> test` now DISCOVERS it (Python imports src/*.py
that carry @tests; PHP discovers @tests docblocks from the tests dir; Node imports
src/*.ts that call tests(); Ruby loads the test/route dirs) and RUNS it via the
inline runner, folding pass/fail into a real process exit code -- 0 when the inline
test passes, non-zero when it fails. The existing external suite (pytest/phpunit/
rspec/file-runner) still runs when present, so a project that keeps tests in tests/
is unaffected. The false CLAUDE.md/docstring claims were corrected to match.
INLINE-DEC-02 (SECURITY + collision): PHP's Testing::discover() used to
require_once EVERY scanned *.php AND eval() the @tests argument expressions --
arbitrary code execution from any scanned file. Discovery is now confined to an
EXPLICIT tests directory (realpath-contained), and the docblock args are parsed as
LITERALS ONLY (no eval; a non-literal arg is refused, never executed). In all four,
discovery imports/loads ONLY files that carry the inline marker (or live in the
tests dir), so scanning never runs an unrelated source file's side effect. The name
collision is resolved by renaming the descriptor builders to expect_* (Python
expect_equal, PHP expectEqual, Ruby Testing.expect_equal, Node expectEqual) --
distinct from the xUnit immediate assert_* (tina4_python.test / Tina4Test /
TestContext), so importing the wrong surface can no longer silently change call
semantics. Python's meta-test snapshots/restores the global @tests registry and
asserts on its own filtered subset, never the global total.
Mutation-proved (macOS, all four): break the CLI's exit-code fold and the
'exits non zero when it fails' case goes RED; drop the inline-marker discovery
filter (Python/Node) or point PHP discover() at the project root / restore the
eval / broaden Ruby cmd_test to load all of src, and the 'does not run a non test
file side effect' case goes RED (the scanned file's side effect runs); re-expose
the colliding assert_equal on the descriptor surface and the 'surfaces are
distinct' case goes RED. Restoring each returns to green.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework and the SAME case name in
each language's own idiom, which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises
and matches.
feature: 132 - Inline testing (wire one tina4 test surface with a real exit code, remove the PHP eval RCE, fix the assertion collision)

invariants.rule: `tina4 <lang> test` discovers a function decorated with the inline @tests/expect_* builders in a project's source and runs it through the inline runner with a REAL process exit code: it exits 0 when the inline test passes and NON-ZERO when it fails. Driven by spawning the real CLI as a child process against a real one-inline-test project and asserting the child's exit status.
invariants.why: The advertised inline-testing flow did not work end-to-end: the CLI ran pytest/phpunit/a file-runner and never the inline runner (Python/PHP/Node), or only the describe/it surface (Ruby), so a green `tina4 test` could execute ZERO of a developer's inline tests (INLINE-ORPHANED-RUNNER + INLINE-SILENT-IGNORE + INLINE-NO-EXITCODE-TAP). Wiring discovery + the runner + a real exit code makes the batteries-included promise real. Mutation-proved: breaking the exit-code fold makes the failing-inline case exit 0, turning it RED.
cases: tina4 test exits zero when the inline test passes
tina4 test exits non zero when the inline test fails

invariants.rule: Running `tina4 <lang> test` never executes a scanned source file's arbitrary code during discovery. A project source file with an observable side effect that is NOT an inline test (Python/Node: it does not carry the inline marker; PHP: it lives outside the tests dir; Ruby: it is a plain src file, not a route/orm/test file) is not imported/required/loaded, so its side effect does not run. PHP additionally parses @tests docblock arguments as LITERALS ONLY -- a function-call argument is never eval'd.
invariants.why: PHP's Testing::discover() require_once'd every scanned *.php AND eval()'d the @tests argument expressions -- arbitrary code execution from any scanned file (INLINE-PHP-EVAL). Confining discovery to an explicit tests directory (realpath-contained), parsing args as literals (no eval), and importing only inline-marked files in all four closes it. Mutation-proved: pointing PHP discover() at the project root (or restoring the eval), or dropping the inline-marker filter in Python/Node, or broadening Ruby cmd_test to load all of src, makes the scanned file's side effect run, turning the case RED.
cases: inline discovery does not run a non test file side effect

invariants.rule: The decorator/descriptor surface exposes expect_* builders (Python expect_equal, PHP Testing::expectEqual, Ruby Testing.expect_equal, Node expectEqual) that RECORD an expectation, and does NOT expose the colliding assert_equal. The xUnit immediate assert_* (tina4_python.test.assert_equal(actual, expected, message) / Tina4Test / Ruby TestContext) remains a separate surface. The descriptor expect_equal builds a spec object; the colliding assert_equal name is absent from the descriptor surface, so importing the wrong one is a loud error, never a silent change of semantics.
invariants.why: In all four, the descriptor builder assert_equal(args, expected) and the xUnit assert_equal(actual, expected, message) exported the SAME name with INCOMPATIBLE signatures, so importing the wrong module silently changed call semantics with no error (INLINE-NAME-COLLISION). Renaming the descriptor builders to expect_* namespaces the two surfaces apart. Mutation-proved: re-exposing assert_equal on the descriptor surface makes the case RED.
cases: the descriptor expect builders and xunit assert are distinct
